# Module Mapping

```{r}
# --- variables and naming ---
input_file <- "./results/05-mahalanobis-distance/KEGG_Pathway_enrichment_mahal4.0_lfc0.50_q0.1_nterms37_ngenes130.tsv"
lookup_col <- "Pathway_Class"
data_table <- read.delim(input_file)
intype <- "Pathway"

show_category <- nrow(data_table)  # plot all categories (nrow(data_table)) or top x
sort_category <- "ID" # Options: "GeneRatio_numeric", "qvalue", "Count", "ID" (KO)

just_the_filename <- basename(input_file)
file_prefix <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(just_the_filename)

# Truncate the prefix so it stops right before "_nterms"
clean_prefix <- sub("_nterms.*", "", file_prefix)

# Output name now uses the truncated clean prefix
output_plot_name <- paste0(clean_prefix, "--", sort_category,"--top_", show_category, "--dotplot.png")

# --- data preparation ---
# Load the data
enrich_df <- read.delim(input_file, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Convert GeneRatio from a fraction string to numeric
if (is.character(enrich_df$GeneRatio)) {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- sapply(enrich_df$GeneRatio, function(x) {
    parts <- as.numeric(strsplit(x, "/")[[1]])
    return(parts[1] / parts[2])
  })
} else {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- enrich_df$GeneRatio
}

# Combine KO ID and Description (e.g., "ko00010: Glycolysis / Gluconeogenesis")
enrich_df <- enrich_df %>%
  mutate(ID_Description = paste0(ID, ": ", Description))

plot_data <- enrich_df %>%
  arrange(qvalue) %>%                    
  head(show_category) %>% # FIX 1: Fixed variable name spelling       
  # FIX 2: Used .data[[ ]] to safely allow dynamic string sorting
  mutate(ID_Description = reorder(ID_Description, .data[[sort_category]]))

# --- plot and export ---
dot_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = GeneRatio_numeric, y = ID_Description)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = qvalue)) + 
  scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue", name = "q-value") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Count") +
  labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio",
    y = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Term"),
    title = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Enrichment Analysis"),
    subtitle = paste("Source:", just_the_filename)
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), # Sightly smaller font for 42 terms
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "darkgray", hjust = 0.5)
  )

# FIX 3: Dynamically adjust height. 42 terms needs more vertical room than 20 terms!
calculated_height <- max(5, show_category * 0.22)

# Save the plot dynamically
ggsave(filename = file.path(results_out, output_plot_name), 
       plot = dot_plot, 
       width = 9, 
       height = calculated_height, 
       dpi = 300)

message("Success! Plot saved as: ", file.path(results_out, output_plot_name))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Parse, extract terms, and calculate unique gene counts per pathway
pathway_frequency_table <- enrich_df %>%
  # Remove any rows where the column in lookup_col is NA
  filter(!is.na(.data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
  
  # Split the combined string pipe (" | ") into separate rows
  # Note: separate_rows() accepts across() or all_of() in newer tidyr versions
  separate_rows(all_of(lookup_col), sep = " \\| ") %>%
  
  # Trim any accidental whitespace
  mutate(across(all_of(lookup_col), trimws)) %>%
  
  # Separate the Map ID from its text description
  # separate() requires !!sym() to evaluate a string variable as a bare column name
  separate(!!sym(lookup_col), into = c("Pathway_ID", "Pathway_Description"), 
           sep = ": ", extra = "merge", fill = "right") %>%
  
  # Separate the slash-delimited genes into individual rows to handle overlaps perfectly
  separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/") %>%
  
  # Group by the pathway to calculate summaries
  group_by(Pathway_ID, Pathway_Description) %>%
  summarise(
    Frequency = n_distinct(ID), 
    Gene_Count = n_distinct(geneID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # --- UPDATED SORTING ---
  arrange(desc(Frequency), desc(Gene_Count))

# 2. View the resulting table in RStudio
print(pathway_frequency_table)
```

```{r setup-target-pathway}
target_pathway <- "Metabolism; Lipid Metabolism" 

# 2. Extract all rows from your enrichment data matching this pathway
pathway_rows <- enrich_df %>%
  # Use .data[[lookup_col]] to reference the column name stored in the variable
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]]))

# 3. Parse and unlist all the gene IDs associated with this pathway
target_genes <- pathway_rows$geneID %>%
  strsplit("/") %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

# 4. Filter your differential expression data for just these pathway genes
pathway_expression <- df_final_clusters %>%
  filter(Gene %in% target_genes) %>%
  select(Gene, model_LFC_06h, model_LFC_24h)

# View the extracted data to make sure it populated correctly
#print(head(pathway_expression))
```

```{r heatmap-and-pathway-map}
# --- heat maps, non-operon ---
# 1. Dynamically find the descriptive name of our target pathway
pathway_desc <- enrich_df %>%
  # Select using all_of() for string variables
  select(all_of(lookup_col)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
  separate_rows(all_of(lookup_col), sep = " \\| ") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(lookup_col), trimws)) %>%
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pull(!!sym(lookup_col)) %>%  # Pull needs a symbol if using Tidyverse evaluation
  sub(".*?: ", "", .) %>% 
  head(1) 

if(length(pathway_desc) == 0 || pathway_desc == "") {
  pathway_desc <- target_pathway
}

# 2. Dynamically name the heatmap output file using the clean name
clean_desc_slug <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "_", tolower(pathway_desc))
clean_desc_slug <- gsub("_+", "_", clean_desc_slug) 
output_heatmap_name <- paste0(clean_prefix, "__", target_pathway, "__", clean_desc_slug, "__heatmap.png")

# 3. Build mapping of Gene to KO(s)
gene_to_ko_mapping <- enrich_df %>%
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]])) %>% # Fixed evaluation here
  select(ID, geneID) %>%
  separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/") %>%
  group_by(geneID) %>%
  summarize(KOs = paste(unique(ID), collapse = "/"), .groups = "drop")

# 4. Extract the numeric suffix from the Gene ID and sort by it
ordered_expression <- pathway_expression %>%
  left_join(gene_to_ko_mapping, by = c("Gene" = "geneID")) %>%
  mutate(Gene_Num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", Gene))) %>%
  arrange(Gene_Num)

# 5. Inject invisible spacer rows where the numeric gap > 5
spaced_expression <- list()
counter <- 1

for(i in 1:nrow(ordered_expression)) {
  spaced_expression[[counter]] <- ordered_expression[i, ]
  counter <- counter + 1
  
  if(i < nrow(ordered_expression)) {
    current_num <- ordered_expression$Gene_Num[i]
    next_num    <- ordered_expression$Gene_Num[i + 1]
    
    if((next_num - current_num) > 5) {
      spacer_row <- data.frame(
        Gene = paste0("SPACER_", current_num), 
        model_LFC_06h = NA,
        model_LFC_24h = NA,
        KOs = "",
        Gene_Num = current_num + 1
      )
      spaced_expression[[counter]] <- spacer_row
      counter <- counter + 1
    }
  }
}

final_spaced_df <- do.call(rbind, spaced_expression)

# 6. Format labels (KEEPING SPACERS UNIQUE) and pivot to long format
heatmap_data <- final_spaced_df %>%
  mutate(
    Gene_KO_Label = ifelse(grepl("SPACER", Gene), Gene, paste0(Gene, " (", KOs, ")"))
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(model_LFC_06h, model_LFC_24h),
    names_to = "Timepoint",
    values_to = "LFC"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Timepoint = sub("model_LFC_", "", Timepoint))

heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label <- factor(heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label, levels = unique(heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label))

# 7. GENERATE DYNAMIC HEATMAP PLOT
pathway_map <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = Timepoint, y = Gene_KO_Label, fill = LFC)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", lwd = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", 
    midpoint = 0, name = "log2 FC", na.value = "transparent" 
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) ifelse(grepl("SPACER", x), "", x)) +
  labs(
    x = "Timepoint", 
    y = paste0("Genes (KEGG ", intype,")"),
    title = pathway_desc, 
    subtitle = paste("Pathway ID:", target_pathway, "| Source:", just_the_filename)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, family = "mono"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "darkgray", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

calc_heatmap_height <- max(4, nrow(final_spaced_df) * 0.22)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(results_out, output_heatmap_name), 
  plot = pathway_map, width = 6.5, height = calc_heatmap_height, dpi = 300
)

message("Success! Spaced heatmap with automated title saved as: ", file.path(results_out, output_heatmap_name))
```


# Visualize operon of genes in lookup_col

```{r}
# 1. Clean up the CSV inputs directly as they are read
static_06h_exp <- read.csv("results/res_06h_exposure.csv") %>%
  select(Gene = gene_id, model_LFC_06h = log2FoldChange, padj_06h = padj)

static_24h_exp <- read.csv("results/res_24h_exposure.csv") %>%
  select(Gene = gene_id, model_LFC_24h = log2FoldChange, padj_24h = padj)


# 2. Clean up the matrix/DESeq objects using position-based selection
static_exp <- res_exposure %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%               
  rownames_to_column(var = "Gene") %>%
  select(Gene, padj_exp = padj)

static_interaction <- res_interaction %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%               
  rownames_to_column(var = "Gene") %>%
  select(Gene, padj_int = padj)


# 3. Consolidate everything into a single, clean join pipeline
anno_operon_stats <- anno_operon_clean %>%
  left_join(static_06h_exp,      by = "Gene") %>%
  left_join(static_24h_exp,      by = "Gene") %>%
  left_join(static_exp,          by = "Gene") %>%
  left_join(static_interaction,  by = "Gene")

# Optional prints if you still need to inspect them in your notebook
print(static_06h_exp)
print(static_24h_exp)
```



```{r extract-operons}
# target_pathway <- "map00280" 

# 2. Extract all rows from your enrichment data matching this pathway
pathway_rows <- enrich_df %>%
  # FIX: Dynamically look up the column name stored inside the lookup_col variable
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]]))

# 3. Parse and unlist all the core gene IDs associated with this pathway
pathway_genes <- pathway_rows$geneID %>%
  strsplit("/") %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

# --- OPERON EXPANSION VIA ANNO_OPERON_STATS ---
# Find which operons contain your pathway genes
target_operons <- anno_operon_stats %>%
  filter(Gene %in% pathway_genes) %>%
  filter(!is.na(operon) & operon != "") %>% # Avoid pulling blank or unassigned operons
  pull(operon) %>%
  unique()

# Pull all genes in those operons + carry through expression data
pathway_expression <- anno_operon_stats %>%
  filter(operon %in% target_operons | Gene %in% pathway_genes) %>%
  select(Gene, model_LFC_06h, model_LFC_24h) %>%
  distinct() # Safety fallback to prevent duplicate rows

# View the extracted data layout
print(head(pathway_expression))
```


```{r}
# --- spaced heatmap with full operons ---

# 1. Dynamically find the descriptive name of our target pathway
pathway_desc <- enrich_df %>%
  # FIX: use all_of() and .data[[]] for dynamic string variable evaluation
  select(all_of(lookup_col)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
  separate_rows(all_of(lookup_col), sep = " \\| ") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(lookup_col), trimws)) %>%
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pull(!!sym(lookup_col)) %>%  # FIX: turn string variable into symbol to pull properly
  sub(".*?: ", "", .) %>% 
  head(1) 

if(length(pathway_desc) == 0 || pathway_desc == "") {
  pathway_desc <- target_pathway
}

# 2. Dynamically name the heatmap output file using the clean slug
clean_desc_slug <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "_", tolower(pathway_desc))
clean_desc_slug <- gsub("_+", "_", clean_desc_slug) 
output_heatmap_name <- paste0(clean_prefix, "__", target_pathway, "__operons__", clean_desc_slug, "__heatmap.png")

# 3. Build mapping of Gene to KO(s) strictly from the core enrichment data
gene_to_ko_mapping <- enrich_df %>%
  filter(grepl(target_pathway, .data[[lookup_col]])) %>% # FIX: evaluate lookup_col
  select(ID, geneID) %>%
  separate_rows(geneID, sep = "/") %>%
  group_by(geneID) %>%
  summarize(KOs = paste(unique(ID), collapse = "/"), .groups = "drop")

# 4. Extract numeric suffix, attach enrichment mapping, and bring in native KO data
ordered_expression <- pathway_expression %>%
  left_join(gene_to_ko_mapping, by = c("Gene" = "geneID")) %>%
  # Bring in the native KO column directly from your master stats frame
  left_join(select(anno_operon_stats, Gene, KO), by = "Gene") %>%
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(Gene_Num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", Gene))) %>%
  arrange(Gene_Num)

# 5. Inject invisible spacer rows where the numeric locus gap > 5
spaced_expression <- list()
counter <- 1

for(i in 1:nrow(ordered_expression)) {
  # Add the actual gene row
  spaced_expression[[counter]] <- ordered_expression[i, ]
  counter <- counter + 1
  
  # If there's a next row, check the distance between their IDs
  if(i < nrow(ordered_expression)) {
    current_num <- ordered_expression$Gene_Num[i]
    next_num    <- ordered_expression$Gene_Num[i + 1]
    
    if((next_num - current_num) > 5) {
      # Create an empty blank spacer row (LFC = NA means it won't color in)
      spacer_row <- data.frame(
        Gene = paste0("SPACER_", current_num), 
        model_LFC_06h = NA,
        model_LFC_24h = NA,
        KOs = NA,
        KO = NA,
        Gene_Num = current_num + 1
      )
      spaced_expression[[counter]] <- spacer_row
      counter <- counter + 1
    }
  }
}

# Bind back into a sequenced data frame
final_spaced_df <- do.call(rbind, spaced_expression)

# 6. Format labels based on annotation origin and pivot to long format
heatmap_data <- final_spaced_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean up empty or missing strings from the native KO database
    KO_clean = ifelse(is.na(KO) | KO == "" | KO == "NA", "no KO", KO),
    
    Gene_KO_Label = case_when(
      grepl("SPACER", Gene) ~ Gene,
      
      # Core pathway hit: Highlight with an asterisk and show enriched KO context
      !is.na(KOs) & KOs != "" ~ paste0(Gene, "* (", KOs, ")"),
      
      # Operon companion gene: Show its native KO from the annotation stats file
      TRUE ~ paste0(Gene, " (", KO_clean, ")")
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(model_LFC_06h, model_LFC_24h),
    names_to = "Timepoint",
    values_to = "LFC"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Timepoint = sub("model_LFC_", "", Timepoint))

# Lock in the factor order strictly based on our genomic sequencing layout
heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label <- factor(heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label, levels = unique(heatmap_data$Gene_KO_Label))

# Generate heatmap
pathway_map <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = Timepoint, y = Gene_KO_Label, fill = LFC)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", lwd = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", 
    midpoint = 0, name = "log2 FC", na.value = "transparent" 
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) ifelse(grepl("SPACER", x), "", x)) +
  labs(
    x = "Timepoint", 
    y = paste0("Genes (KEGG ", intype,") [* = Core Pathway]"),
    title = pathway_desc, 
    subtitle = paste("Pathway ID:", target_pathway, "| Source:", just_the_filename)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, family = "mono"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "darkgray", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# 8. Dynamically scale the output image height based on the row and spacer counts
calc_heatmap_height <- max(4, nrow(final_spaced_df) * 0.22)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(results_out, output_heatmap_name), 
  plot = pathway_map, width = 6.5, height = calc_heatmap_height, dpi = 300
)

message("Success! Operon-expanded spaced heatmap saved to: ", file.path(results_out, output_heatmap_name))
```

# Pathway Visualization
# Module Mapping

```{r}
# --- variables and naming ---
input_file <- "./results/05-mahalanobis-distance/KEGG_Pathway_enrichment_mahal4.0_lfc0.50_q0.1_nterms37_ngenes130.tsv"
lookup_col <- "Pathway_Class"
data_table <- read.delim(input_file)
intype <- "Pathway"

show_category <- nrow(data_table)  # plot all categories (nrow(data_table)) or top x
sort_category <- "ID" # Options: "GeneRatio_numeric", "qvalue", "Count", "ID" (KO)

just_the_filename <- basename(input_file)
file_prefix <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(just_the_filename)

# Truncate the prefix so it stops right before "_nterms"
clean_prefix <- sub("_nterms.*", "", file_prefix)

# Output name now uses the truncated clean prefix
output_plot_name <- paste0(clean_prefix, "--", sort_category,"--top_", show_category, "--dotplot.png")

# --- data preparation ---
enrich_df <- read.delim(input_file, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Convert GeneRatio from a fraction string to numeric
if (is.character(enrich_df$GeneRatio)) {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- sapply(enrich_df$GeneRatio, function(x) {
    parts <- as.numeric(strsplit(x, "/")[[1]])
    return(parts[1] / parts[2])
  })
} else {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- enrich_df$GeneRatio
}

# Combine KO ID and Description
enrich_df <- enrich_df %>%
  mutate(ID_Description = paste0(ID, ": ", Description))

# --- FILTER BY MAP NUMBERS ---
  plot_data <- enrich_df %>%
    # 1. Clear out NAs from your dynamic lookup column
    filter(!is.na(.data[[lookup_col]])) %>%
    
    # 2. Extract numeric map IDs from the 'ID' column (e.g., "ko04066" -> 4066)
    mutate(Map_Num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", ID))) %>%
    
    # 3. FIX: Blanket filter out all exclusively eukaryotic ranges (4000 to 5999)
    filter(!(Map_Num >= 4000 & Map_Num <= 5999)) %>%
    
    # 4. Sort and pull your top categories
    arrange(qvalue) %>%                    
    head(show_category) %>%       
    mutate(ID_Description = reorder(ID_Description, .data[[sort_category]]))
# --- plot and export ---
dot_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = GeneRatio_numeric, y = ID_Description)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = qvalue)) + 
  scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue", name = "q-value") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Count") +
  labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio",
    y = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Term"),
    title = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Enrichment Analysis"),
    subtitle = paste("Source:", just_the_filename)
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "darkgray", hjust = 0.5)
  )

# Dynamically adjust height based on the filtered dataset row count
calculated_height <- max(5, nrow(plot_data) * 0.22)

# Save the plot dynamically
ggsave(filename = file.path(results_out, output_plot_name), 
       plot = dot_plot, 
       width = 9, 
       height = calculated_height, 
       dpi = 300)

message("Success! Plot saved as: ", file.path(results_out, output_plot_name))
```

```{r}
# --- variables and naming ---
input_file <- "./results/05-mahalanobis-distance/KEGG_Reaction_enrichment_mahal4.0_lfc0.50_q0.1_nterms93_ngenes58.tsv"
data_table <- read.delim(input_file)
intype <- "Rxn"

# ADDED/UPDATED: Filtering parameters
padj_threshold <- 0.05  # Set your p.adj threshold cutoff here
max_terms      <- 20    # NEW: Max number of terms you want to display on the plot

# Dynamic categorical selection
sort_category <- "ID" # Options: "GeneRatio_numeric", "padj", "Count", "ID" (KO)

just_the_filename <- basename(input_file)
file_prefix <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(just_the_filename)

# Truncate the prefix so it stops right before "_nterms"
clean_prefix <- sub("_nterms.*", "", file_prefix)

# --- data preparation ---
# Load the data safely
enrich_df <- read.delim(input_file, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Auto-detect column naming variant for p.adj
if ("p.adj" %in% colnames(enrich_df)) {
  enrich_df$padj <- as.numeric(enrich_df$p.adj)
} else if ("padj" %in% colnames(enrich_df)) {
  enrich_df$padj <- as.numeric(enrich_df$padj)
} else if ("qvalue" %in% colnames(enrich_df)) {
  enrich_df$padj <- as.numeric(enrich_df$qvalue) 
} else {
  stop("Could not find a p.adj, padj, or qvalue column!")
}

# Convert GeneRatio from a fraction string to numeric safely
if ("GeneRatio" %in% colnames(enrich_df) && is.character(enrich_df$GeneRatio)) {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- sapply(enrich_df$GeneRatio, function(x) {
    x_clean <- gsub(" ", "", x) 
    parts <- as.numeric(strsplit(x_clean, "/")[[1]])
    if(length(parts) == 2 && !any(is.na(parts))) {
      return(parts[1] / parts[2])
    } else {
      return(NA)
    }
  })
} else if ("GeneRatio" %in% colnames(enrich_df)) {
  enrich_df$GeneRatio_numeric <- as.numeric(enrich_df$GeneRatio)
} else {
  stop("Could not find 'GeneRatio' column.")
}

# Truncate Description at first ';' or 50 characters
enrich_df <- enrich_df %>%
  mutate(Description_clean = sub(";.*", "", Description)) %>%
  mutate(Description_clean = substr(Description_clean, 1, 50)) %>%
  mutate(ID_Description = paste0(ID, ": ", Description_clean))

# Ensure Count is explicitly numeric 
enrich_df$Count <- as.numeric(enrich_df$Count)

# --- FILTER & SORT PIPELINE ---
plot_data <- enrich_df %>%
  # 1. Drop true NA rows across essential visual spaces
  filter(!is.na(GeneRatio_numeric), !is.na(Count), !is.na(padj)) %>%
  # 2. Filter on your padj threshold first
  filter(padj <= padj_threshold) %>%
  # 3. Sort strictly by your chosen variable (e.g., "ID")
  arrange(.data[[sort_category]]) %>%
  # 4. Limit to the maximum number of terms specified
  head(max_terms)

# Set dynamic category count for naming based on what survived the cut
show_category <- nrow(plot_data)

# Output name accounts for the thresholds and caps
output_plot_name <- paste0(clean_prefix, "--", sort_category,"--padj_", padj_threshold, "--top_", show_category, "--dotplot.png")

# Explicitly lock in the y-axis order exactly based on the alphabetical ID sort order
plot_data$ID_Description <- factor(plot_data$ID_Description, levels = unique(plot_data$ID_Description))

# --- DEBUG PRINT ---
message("Rows to plot after padj filtering and max cap: ", nrow(plot_data))
if (nrow(plot_data) > 0) {
  print(head(plot_data[, c("ID_Description", "GeneRatio_numeric", "Count", "padj")]))
} else {
  stop("Error: 0 rows passed your filtering criteria!")
}

# --- plot and export ---
dot_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = GeneRatio_numeric, y = ID_Description)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, color = padj)) +   
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.1))) + 
  scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue", name = "p.adj") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Count") +
  labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio",
    y = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Term"),
    title = paste0("KEGG ", intype," Enrichment Analysis"),
    subtitle = paste("Source:", just_the_filename)
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5), 
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, color = "darkgray", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 10, l = 20, unit = "pt") 
  )

# Dynamically adjust height to accommodate the capped row count cleanly
calculated_height <- max(5, nrow(plot_data) * 0.25)

# Save the plot
ggsave(filename = file.path(results_out, output_plot_name), 
       plot = dot_plot, 
       width = 11,               
       height = calculated_height, 
       limitsize = FALSE,        
       dpi = 300)

message("Success! Plot saved as: ", file.path(results_out, output_plot_name))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# 1. Clean and build the Reaction -> Module Edge List
edges_modules <- enrich_df %>%
  # Keep only reaction ID and the Module string
  select(from = ID, Group_Raw = Modules) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Group_Raw) & Group_Raw != "" & Group_Raw != "NA") %>%
  # Split pipe-separated modules into individual rows
  separate_rows(Group_Raw, sep = " \\| ") %>%
  mutate(Group_Raw = trimws(Group_Raw)) %>%
  # Extract code (Mxxxxx) and descriptive name
  separate(Group_Raw, into = c("to_id", "to_name"), sep = ": ", 
           extra = "merge", fill = "right") %>%
  mutate(Type = "Module")

# 2. Clean and build the Reaction -> Pathway Edge List
edges_pathways <- enrich_df %>%
  select(from = ID, Group_Raw = Pathways) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Group_Raw) & Group_Raw != "" & Group_Raw != "NA") %>%
  separate_rows(Group_Raw, sep = " \\| ") %>%
  mutate(Group_Raw = trimws(Group_Raw)) %>%
  separate(Group_Raw, into = c("to_id", "to_name"), sep = ": ", 
           extra = "merge", fill = "right") %>%
  # BLACKLIST: Drop global/overview pathways (rn01100, rn01120, etc.)
  filter(!to_id %in% c("rn01100", "rn01120")) %>%
  mutate(Type = "Pathway")

# 3. Combine into a master edge list
network_edges <- bind_rows(edges_modules, edges_pathways) %>%
  # The 'to' column for the network needs to use the unique ID code
  mutate(to = to_id) %>%
  select(from, to, to_name, Type)

# Quick check of the edge architecture
print(head(network_edges))
```

```{r}
# GENERATE UNIFIED NODE LIST WITH METADATA


# Reaction Nodes Metadata
nodes_reactions <- enrich_df %>%
  filter(ID %in% network_edges$from) %>%
  select(node_id = ID, qvalue, Count) %>%
  mutate(
    Node_Type = "Reaction",
    Label = node_id,
    Node_Size = 3, 
    Fill_Value = qvalue
  )

# Group Nodes (Modules/Pathways) Metadata
group_counts <- network_edges %>%
  group_by(to, to_name, Type) %>%
  summarise(Enriched_Reaction_Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

nodes_groups <- group_counts %>%
  select(node_id = to, Label = to_name, Node_Type = Type, Node_Size = Enriched_Reaction_Count) %>%
  mutate(
    qvalue = NA,
    Count = NA,
    Fill_Value = NA
  )

# Combine both sets of nodes
master_nodes <- bind_rows(nodes_reactions, nodes_groups)

# MAKE GRAPH OBJECT

clean_graph_obj <- tbl_graph(nodes = master_nodes, edges = network_edges, directed = FALSE) %>%
  # Activate the nodes layer to calculate degree
  activate(nodes) %>%
  # Calculate the number of connections for each node
  mutate(node_degree = centrality_degree()) %>%
  # CRITICAL FILTER: Keep only nodes that have 1 or more connections
  filter(node_degree > 1)

# plot clean network

network_plot_clean <- ggraph(clean_graph_obj, layout = "stress") + 
  geom_edge_link(aes(color = Type), alpha = 0.2, width = 0.4) +
  geom_node_point(aes(shape = Node_Type, size = Node_Size, color = Fill_Value)) +
  
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "gold", na.value = "lightgray", 
                       name = "Reaction q-value") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2.5, 9), name = "Reaction Count / Size") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Reaction" = 16, "Module" = 15, "Pathway" = 17),
                     name = "Node Classification") +
  
  # Repel text labels cleanly, only showing pathway/module descriptors
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(Node_Type != "Reaction", Label, "")), 
                 repel = TRUE, size = 2.5, fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 30) +
  
  theme_graph() +
  labs(
    title = "Connected KEGG Reaction Crosstalk Network",
    subtitle = "Orphan nodes removed; showing shared reaction architectures"
  )

print(network_plot_clean)

ggsave(file.path(results_out,"networkmap-rxn-pathway-module.png"))
```

```{r}
  filter(component == which.max(tabulate(component)))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PARSE GENE WEIGHTS FROM ENRICH_DF
# ==============================================================================
# Count how many individual genes are assigned to each reaction row
enrich_weighted <- enrich_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean and split the geneID column (assumes it is slash '/' or comma separated)
    # Adjust sep if your geneID uses a different delimiter (e.g., ", " or ";")
    Gene_Count = str_count(geneID, "[^/,;]+") 
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 2. GENERATE GENE-WEIGHTED MODULE EDGES & NODES
# ==============================================================================
edges_mod_weighted <- enrich_weighted %>%
  select(from = ID, Group_Raw = Modules, Gene_Count) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Group_Raw) & Group_Raw != "" & Group_Raw != "NA") %>%
  separate_rows(Group_Raw, sep = " \\| ") %>%
  mutate(Group_Raw = trimws(Group_Raw)) %>%
  separate(Group_Raw, into = c("to", "to_name"), sep = ": ", extra = "merge", fill = "right")

# Create Module Nodes where size is determined by total GENE WEIGHT
nodes_mod_weighted <- edges_mod_weighted %>%
  group_by(to, to_name) %>%
  # SUM the gene counts instead of counting the rows of reactions
  summarise(Total_Gene_Weight = sum(Gene_Count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  select(node_id = to, Label = to_name, Node_Size = Total_Gene_Weight) %>%
  mutate(Node_Type = "Module", Fill_Value = NA)

# Base reaction nodes with their specific gene counts as node sizes
nodes_reactions_weighted <- enrich_weighted %>%
  filter(ID %in% edges_mod_weighted$from) %>%
  select(node_id = ID, qvalue, Gene_Count) %>%
  mutate(
    Node_Type = "Reaction",
    Label = node_id,
    Node_Size = Gene_Count, # Reaction dots scale by how many genes drive them
    Fill_Value = qvalue
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. BUILD THE GENE-WEIGHTED GIANT COMPONENT
# ==============================================================================
master_nodes_weighted <- bind_rows(nodes_reactions_weighted, nodes_mod_weighted)

graph_mod_weighted <- tbl_graph(nodes = master_nodes_weighted, 
                                edges = edges_mod_weighted, directed = FALSE) %>%
  activate(nodes) %>%
  mutate(
    node_degree = centrality_degree(),
    component = group_components()
  ) %>%
  filter(node_degree > 0) %>%
  filter(component == which.max(tabulate(component)))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PLOT GENE-WEIGHTED NETWORK AND AUTOSAVE
# ==============================================================================
plot_modules_weighted <- ggraph(graph_mod_weighted, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(color = "grey85", alpha = 0.5, width = 0.3) +
  
  # Sizes now natively scale to Gene Weights!
  geom_node_point(aes(shape = Node_Type, size = Node_Size, color = Fill_Value)) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "orange", na.value = "deepskyblue4", name = "Reaction q-value") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2.5, 12), name = "Gene Abundance / Weight") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Reaction" = 16, "Module" = 15), name = "Node Type") +
  
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(Node_Type == "Reaction", Label, "")),
                 color = "grey65", size = 1.8, fontface = "plain", repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = 50) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(Node_Type == "Module", Label, "")),
                 color = "black", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = 20) +
  theme_graph() +
  labs(
    title = "Gene-Weighted Reaction-to-Module Network", 
    subtitle = "Hub sizes scale by total gene count across pathways"
  )

# Autosave out to your directory

weighted_out_path <- file.path(results_out, "kegg_gene_weighted_module_network.png")

ggsave(
  filename = weighted_out_path, plot = plot_modules_weighted,
  width = 12, height = 12, dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
message("Success! Gene-weighted network saved to: ", weighted_out_path)
```
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# PRINT TOP ENRICHED ELEMENTS BY GENE CONTRIBUTION
# ==============================================================================
library(tibble)

# Extract node data from the giant component graph object
node_data <- graph_mod_weighted %>% 
  activate(nodes) %>% 
  as_tibble()

# Set 'X' to however many top nodes you want to view
top_x <- 12

cat("\n=== TOP", top_x, "MODULE HUBS BY GENE CONTRIBUTION ===\n")
top_modules <- node_data %>%
  filter(Node_Type == "Module") %>%
  arrange(desc(Node_Size)) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_x) %>%
  select(Module_ID = node_id, Module_Name = Label, Total_Gene_Weight = Node_Size)

print(as.data.frame(top_modules), row.names = FALSE)


cat("\n=== TOP", top_x, "INDIVIDUAL REACTIONS BY GENE CONTRIBUTION ===\n")
top_reactions <- node_data %>%
  filter(Node_Type == "Reaction") %>%
  arrange(desc(Node_Size)) %>%
  slice_head(n = top_x) %>%
  select(Reaction_ID = node_id, qvalue, Gene_Count = Node_Size)

print(as.data.frame(top_reactions), row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}


# ==============================================================================
# BUILD THE INCLUSIVE GENE-WEIGHTED METABOLIC GRAPH
# ==============================================================================
graph_mod_inclusive <- tbl_graph(nodes = bind_rows(nodes_reactions_weighted, nodes_mod_weighted), 
                                 edges = edges_mod_weighted, directed = FALSE) %>%
  activate(nodes) %>%
  mutate(
    node_degree = centrality_degree(),
    component = group_components()
  ) %>%
  # Remove completely unlinked singletons (0 connections)
  filter(node_degree > 0) %>%
  
  # CRITERIA: Keep the giant component OR any smaller satellite component 
  # that contains a highly significant reaction (qvalue < 0.05)
  group_by(component) %>%
  mutate(
    is_giant = (component == which.max(tabulate(component))),
    has_high_sig = any(Node_Type == "Reaction" & Fill_Value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is_giant | has_high_sig)

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT WITH AN ISLAND-FRIENDLY MULTI-COMPONENT LAYOUT ("nicely")
# ==============================================================================
plot_modules_inclusive <- ggraph(graph_mod_inclusive, layout = "nicely") +
  # Light background lines
  geom_edge_link(color = "grey85", alpha = 0.5, width = 0.3) +
  
  # Nodes mapped to your gene weights and q-values
  geom_node_point(aes(shape = Node_Type, size = Node_Size, color = Fill_Value)) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "orange", na.value = "deepskyblue4", name = "Reaction q-value") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2.5, 12), name = "Gene Abundance / Weight") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Reaction" = 16, "Module" = 15), name = "Node Type") +
  
  # Faded plain text for Reaction codes
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(Node_Type == "Reaction", Label, "")),
                 color = "grey65", size = 1.8, fontface = "plain", repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = 50) +
  
  # Bold dark text for the Module Hubs
  geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(Node_Type == "Module", Label, "")),
                 color = "black", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = 20) +
  
  theme_graph() +
  labs(
    title = "Inclusive Reaction-to-Module Network", 
    subtitle = "Central fatty acid core with orbiting high-fold-change satellite pathways"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# AUTOSAVE TO CENTRAL RESULTS DIRECTORY
# ==============================================================================
inclusive_out_path <- file.path(results_out, "kegg_inclusive_module_network.png")

ggsave(
  filename = inclusive_out_path, 
  plot = plot_modules_inclusive,
  width = 14, 
  height = 14, 
  dpi = 300, 
  bg = "white"
)

message("Success! Inclusive network layout saved to: ", inclusive_out_path)
```
